positive_evidence: Large tactical battles with different units and commanders strongly support planning, adaptation and learnable strategic mastery.
New scenarios and larger battlefields provide changing constraints and explicit mission goals instead of one static skirmish loop.
negative_evidence: Realistic large-scale control can become management-heavy if missions demand more setup than meaningful tactical change.

positive_evidence: Artifacts, crafted pickaxes and a permanent skill tree provide visible numerical development.
negative_evidence: The game explicitly centers on incremental mining and repeated material accumulation, a direct structural conflict with the profile's strong dislike of static repetition.

positive_evidence: Playing a prince facing invasion and a stagnant court gives choices clear political stakes and narrative direction.
Consequential decisions fit the user's interest in stories where actions matter rather than merely following a fixed sequence.
negative_evidence: The available candidate evidence says little about active gameplay depth, so the match relies substantially on narrative execution.

positive_evidence: Constructing vessels, settlements and stations provides highly visible long-term progression and creative system mastery.
The mysteries of Empyrion give galactic exploration an authored hook beyond building for its own sake.
negative_evidence: A true space sandbox creates major direction and routine-resource risks for a profile that prefers clear next goals.

positive_evidence: Direct zombie combat in an open island provides active mechanical engagement and an immediately understandable survival objective.
The tropical outbreak setting gives exploration a distinctive contrast between vacation environment and horror.
negative_evidence: Open-world errands and repeated zombie encounters can become repetitive if progression does not keep changing combat choices.

positive_evidence: Using varied spells to hit a vandalism target while evading magical guardians creates a clear cooperative tactical problem.
Playing mischievous wizard minions invading rival towers gives the horror-coop format a distinctive comic dark-fantasy identity.
negative_evidence: Replay value depends on towers, spells and monsters changing enough to prevent the same sabotage routine from dominating.

positive_evidence: Combat, creature taming and crafted weaponry provide several interacting ways to develop power and experiment with play.
Outlandish locals and the world-conquering villain add character, humor and clear narrative purpose to the open exploration.
negative_evidence: Crafting can become routine if gathering occupies too much time between new creatures, characters and combat situations.

positive_evidence: Team-based tactical shooting can strongly reward positioning, coordination and mechanical execution, all durable positive signals in the profile.
A story-rich battlefield framing gives combat emotional and narrative context rather than presenting isolated competitive rounds.
negative_evidence: The fit depends on teamwork and encounter design staying meaningful rather than devolving into repeated firefights.

positive_evidence: Being massively outnumbered creates a strategic puzzle where survival depends on understanding systems and choosing battles intelligently.
The lost war against machine forces supplies clear stakes and a distinctive science-fiction strategic identity.
negative_evidence: Very large-scale strategy may impose substantial learning overhead before the tactical possibilities become readable.

positive_evidence: High-adrenaline arcade shooting rewards movement, aim and threat management with immediate feedback.
Cooperative support allows the same mechanical loop to become a meaningful shared action experience.
negative_evidence: Classic mass-enemy shooting can become repetitive when arenas mainly increase enemy count rather than changing decisions.

positive_evidence: Fast arcade FPS play creates a clear mechanical mastery loop around movement, aiming and enemy prioritization.
Large cooperative support can turn straightforward shooting into coordinated shared play.
negative_evidence: The classic formula offers limited evidence of development variety and risks repetitive wave combat.

positive_evidence: Fast first-person combat gives immediate execution feedback and strong opportunity for movement-and-aim mastery.
A campaign prequel supplies forward momentum instead of making the action purely score-driven.
negative_evidence: Its core identity remains mass-enemy shooting, so long-term fit depends on encounter and weapon variety.

positive_evidence: Third-person hack-and-slash combat offers active execution and character-based mastery in cooperative encounters.
Using the RWBY cast gives the action recognizable character identity and supports meaningful team play with friends.
negative_evidence: The co-op combat loop may become repetitive if missions and enemy groups do not create enough new tactical situations.

positive_evidence: Ultra-responsive sword fighting and dual-stick shooting strongly match the user's enjoyment of difficult but learnable execution mastery.
The simple objective of defeating jailers to earn freedom gives each demanding fight clear purpose and momentum.
negative_evidence: Boss-focused structure can require repeated attempts, though that repetition is mitigated when each failure teaches a readable pattern.

positive_evidence: The question of whether an emotional robot has a soul provides a strong character-centered science-fiction theme.
The premise directly supports the profile's interest in relationships, emotions and authored narrative identity.
negative_evidence: The candidate evidence provides almost no active gameplay signal, so sustained fit depends heavily on character writing and story pacing.

positive_evidence: The historical psychological-horror framing suggests a serious authored atmosphere and personal story.
negative_evidence: Current candidate evidence does not establish enough active gameplay, progression, clear mystery structure or other durable strengths to prove moderate fit for this profile.

positive_evidence: Building and surviving in Hyboria offer visible development and multiple systems to learn alone or cooperatively.
The Conan setting supplies a strong fantasy identity and adventure context to the survival sandbox.
negative_evidence: The open-ended survive-build-dominate structure can become grindy, repetitive and weakly directed over a long campaign.

positive_evidence: Missing animals and strange villagers create an immediate mystery with a concrete reason to investigate the village.
The ordinary shepherd role turning terrifying provides a specific horror identity and escalating narrative hook.
negative_evidence: The candidate evidence gives limited proof of mechanical depth, so fit depends on investigation and story progression staying active.

positive_evidence: Preparing varied orders under time pressure creates a clear execution-and-coordination mastery loop with immediate feedback.
Couch cooperation makes communication and role division central to success, directly supporting meaningful shared play.
negative_evidence: Repeated kitchen tasks could become tiring if changing layouts and recipes do not sufficiently alter coordination problems.

positive_evidence: Switching between space simulation, pirate hunting and on-foot adventure creates unusually strong activity variation and multiple mastery layers.
Derelicts, shady characters and space-bar interactions give exploration narrative and social texture beyond a pure flight sandbox.
negative_evidence: The open galaxy can still produce weak direction if optional activities overwhelm clearer authored goals.
